thread:
maria: quick security check — need confirmation for a few things before the SOC audit next week:
1) TLS versions enforced on public API and internal mesh
2) Who owns KMS key rotations for prod, and the approval flow
3) Are any PII fields or client IPs leaking into our logs (prod access logs + app logs)?

ajay: @maria short answers: public endpoints = TLS1.3 only at ALB (no 1.2 fallback). internal service-mesh uses mTLS via cert-manager, minimum TLS1.3 config.
	maria: thanks — can you point to the config?

ajay: ALB listener config is in infra repo: `infra/loadbalancers/alb/main.tf` — we set `ssl_policy = "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2023-07"` and explicitly disabled older ciphers. For verification you can run: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -tls1_3`
	leo: internal mesh: `istio` config stored in `infra/mesh/`. We pin `TLS_MIN_VERSION: TLSv1.3` in the `Gateway` and have `peerAuthn` mTLS enforced cluster-wide. No 1.2 fallback.
	katie: KMS/key ownership — prod CMK alias `alias/redwood-prod-kms` is owned by group `sec-crypto` (IAM path `/groups/sec-crypto`). Rotation schedule: automated yearly rotation by default, but we have a monthly key-rotation job for ephemeral data keys used in inference cache.
	maria: who has permission to trigger rotation or rotate early? we need an approval flow documented.
	katie: only members of `sec-crypto` + `eng-sre` can call `RotateKey` or `ScheduleKeyRotation`. We enforce 2-person approval in the internal runbook via a GitHub PR that updates the rotation tag in `infra/keys/rotation.yaml` and requires reviews from `sec-crypto` and `eng-sre` teams.
	ajay: note: the CMK itself is an AWS KMS key (not an external HSM). For highest compliance customers we support an HSM-backed key using AWS CloudHSM — that is used only for Private deployments (VPC) when customers request BYOK.
	maria: logs — are client IPs or full X-Forwarded-For stored anywhere unredacted?
	leo: access logs on the ALB have the full client IP but those logs are sent to S3 with lifecycle + restricted ACLs. We redact IPs in app-level telemetry before shipping to our metrics pipeline. For the access logs we set an IAM policy so only `logging-processor` and `sec-ops` role can read raw logs. We also run a daily job that replaces IPs with truncated CIDR in the analytics dataset: example job in `infra/logging/redaction/job.yaml` includes a sed transform: `s/([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/\1.0.0/g`
	maria: good. Are those redaction jobs audited? need proof for SOC.
	katie: yes — every redaction run posts a signed entry to CloudTrail and we have a nightly commit in `infra/logging/redaction/` showing the job run ID and checksum. We also emit a metric `redaction.job.success` to the console dashboard.
	deploy-bot: [deploy] redaction-job v2.3.1 completed on prod at 2025-06-20T02:12:34Z :white_check_mark:
	maria: ok — last thing: TLS cert rotation for ALB and mesh. Who rotates and what's the cadence?
	ajay: ALB certs are ACM-managed for public domains, auto-renewed by AWS (we monitor expiry via `cert-monitor`). Mesh certs are handled by cert-manager with certs rotated every 60 days. For emergency rotation we have a `cert-rotation` runbook that `eng-sre` can trigger — the runbook includes a canary rollout: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/api --namespace=canary` then `kubectl rollout restart --namespace=prod` after 10min.
	maria: perfect. can someone drop links to the runbooks/configs in this thread? i'll add to the audit tracker.
	katie: links: infra repo → `infra/keys/rotation.yaml` (PR approvals), logging redaction job → `infra/logging/redaction/`, cert runbook → `docs/runbooks/cert-rotation.md`. I'll add to the SOC ticket.
	maria: thanks all — @ajay @katie @leo please add any missing bits into the SOC checklist. merging to tracker by EOD. :white_check_mark:
